## Textbook

We will use three main textbooks for the course all of which are freely available online. You will not be expected to purchase paper copies. 

[Hello Data Science: A Friendly Introduction with Applications](https://hellodata.science/) by Mine Doğucu, Catalina Medina, and Alma Castro

[Modern Data Science with R](https://mdsr-book.github.io/mdsr2e) by Benjamin S. Baumer, Daniel T. Kaplan, and Nicholas J. Horton. 

[R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) by Hadley Wickham, Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel, and Garrett Grolemund

## Programming Tools

**R and RStudio** We will use the R language which is a popular programming language used by statisticians and data scientists. We will use RStudio interface while using the R language.

**Git and GitHub** We will use GitHub for version control with git. We will soon learn what version control means.

## Other Software

We will use [an online forum]({{< var course.discussion >}}) where you can ask and answer questions. Please read [guidelines](03-policies.html#online-discussion) for the online forum. I will also make announcements using this forum. It is your responsibility to check the forum on a regular basis thus make sure to have appropriate notifications turned on.

We will use [Gradescope]({{< var course.gradescope >}}) for some of the assignments. You will get instructions on how to use Gradescope.

We will use [Poll EV](https://www.huit.harvard.edu/poll-everywhere) for conducting in-class quizzes.


We will use [Canvas]({{< var course.lms >}}) for keeping track of grades.
